PHASE 02 · THE VOCABULARY

Three terms. Three meanings

THE PERSONEntrepreneurIdentifies a problem and accepts the risk of solving it
THE PROCESSEntrepreneurshipBuilding, launching and running the solution
THE MINDSETEntrepreneurialA way of thinking and acting that anyone can develop

The word comes from the French “entreprendre”, meaning “to undertake”: to take responsibility and act.

PHASE 05 · THE MINDSET

Five shifts in thinking

Complaint→Opportunity
“I need capital first”→“What resources do I have?”
Failure→Feedback
“It is not my job”→“I take ownership”
Accepting the status quo→Asking “why?” and “what if?”

PHASE 06 · THE ROLES

Entrepreneur vs businessman

CREATES THE VENTUREEntrepreneur
  • Starts with an unmet need or new idea
  • Asks: “What should exist?”
  • Accepts high, uncertain risk
  • Builds something new
OPERATES THE BUSINESSBusinessman
  • Runs a proven model
  • Asks: “How do we run this efficiently?”
  • Manages measured, known risk
  • Targets stable profit

Neither role is superior. Strong leaders can move between both.

Problem spottingDAILYImprove your study systemCAREERDoctor reduces waiting time
Financial senseDAILYPlan your pocket moneyCAREEREngineer compares project costs
CommunicationDAILYPresent ideas clearlyCAREERPitch a proposal to a client
ResilienceDAILYRecover after a poor resultCAREERRebuild after a failed project
InitiativeDAILYStart a study groupCAREERLead a new project
TrustDAILYSupport your classmatesCAREERBuild a network of mentors
IntrapreneurAn employee who acts like an entrepreneur inside an organisation, identifying problems and driving solutions. Hospitals, companies and armed forces value this.

PHASE 08 · THE EXECUTION

Six steps. Keep the sequence

01Identify a real problem
02Interview ten potential customers
03Build a minimum viable version
04Price it using cost and margin
05Win your first ten customers
06Collect feedback and improve

Customers buy outcomes, not features: “Hot tea from the bus stop to the last class.”

PHASE 11 · THE MISSION

Your plan starts tonight

Your missionKeep a problem log. Record one real problem each day for seven days. On day eight, choose one and take one small, practical step toward solving it.

“You do not need permission, capital or a degree to begin. You need a problem, a first step and the discipline to continue.”
